domain_label: AI Design (T8) — The Flux Generative Method & The Producibility Bridge
purpose: A method for running the owner's Flux generative-design pipeline for the 3-article California knitwear line (A1 cotton-blend 12GG core, A2 fine-acrylic 7-12GG value/youth driver, A3 thin merino/lambswool Nov-Feb premium capsule) so that pretty images become producible garments and never an un-buildable tech pack: it fixes what Flux IS in this pipeline (an idea and fashion-photo content engine, not a knit compiler) and the expensive mistake that framing prevents, gives the eight-slot prompt skeleton that bakes the four upstream constraints (<=2-4 colours, 12GG warm-California weight, few-seam linker throughput, anti-pill) into every render, sets the guidance-distilled snapshot params and the positive-phrasing and seed-locked iteration discipline, supplies a reusable fill-in template and ready-to-run A1/A2/A3 prompts, builds the honest image-to-producible bridge (the four buildability inputs a pixel cannot give mapped to who fills them, the three traps Flux renders wrong, and the central UNKNOWN of AI-design->knit-program autonomy on our fabrics), reconciles trend ingestion into a four-drop calendar, and scores any design's producibility-readiness as constraints-met x traps-avoided x PPS-validated. Every param is a labelled snapshot, the AI-autonomy claim is held UNKNOWN, and AI is treated as a multiplier on a human programmer plus a physical swatch, never a substitute.
assumptions: the owner runs the Flux pipeline himself on a Flux-dev/pro/schnell-class endpoint; all guidance/steps/dimensions/seed values are snapshot starting points to re-confirm on the live model version, never fixed constants

Flux sits upstream of the CAD/flat-knit programmer (machines node) at the idea/look step of the generative-design->simulation->virtual-sampling chain; it is not the program and produces no stitch count, gauge, count, measurement, or shrinkage behaviour

the four design constraints (<=2-4 launch colours from the dye-lot MOQ, 12GG warm-California weight, few-seam linker-throughput discipline, anti-pill on acrylic) are inherited as fixed from yarn and machines and are encoded into the prompt rather than re-derived here

every buildability number (yarn count, true GG/density, stitch-count grade, finished measurements/shrinkage) is filled downstream by T2 yarn, the T3 CAD programmer, the sizing math, and a physical PPS swatch that is the ground truth, never read off a render

trend specifics for Central-Valley youth in mid-2026 are UNKNOWN and refused, not fabricated; channels are estimates, and the gap is closed by a listening loop plus pop-up recon plus own-channel sell-through, not by a guess
AI design->knit-program autonomy on our acrylic/cotton/merino fabrics is UNKNOWN and must be tested not assumed; until proven, a human programmer plus a physical swatch always close the loop
exclusions: the sizing and grading math itself (finished-measurement base, linear grade rule, inch-to-stitch translation, shrinkage offset) - covered by the sizing/grading KB; this KB only references where the grade is filled into the bridge

the line architecture and per-article design judgement (why exactly three, the texture-over-colour rule, the loud-front/evergreen-behind rule) as a standalone deliverable - inherited from the design deep-dive and used, not re-argued
yarn sourcing, count selection, MOQ, dye-lot, and anti-pill spec mechanics - covered by the yarn KB; used here only as the buildability inputs the bridge hands off
machine selection, programmer hiring, and linker economics - covered by the machines KB; used here only as the producibility ceiling and the autonomy UNKNOWN

brand naming, channel, price ladder, and the legal clearance gate as standalone work - covered by the brand/market KB; only the right-of-publicity/Lanham/Class-25 exposure as it applies to AI renders is carried here as a guardrail
the landed-cost and contribution-after-CAC unit economics - covered by the logistics/unit-economics KB

glossary.definition: The framing that Flux is a near-zero-marginal-cost visual-ideation, mood, and content engine sitting upstream of the CAD/flat-knit programmer, NOT a knit compiler, gauge calculator, or grading engine; a Flux image carries design intent but no stitch count, GG, yarn count, measurement, or shrinkage, so it de-risks the idea but never the make.

The ordered descriptive-prose prompt scaffold (garment/fibre, construction/stitch/GG, silhouette/fit, colour/blend, detail, styling, shot-type, photography/light) in which each slot pulls a specific upstream vocabulary and the four design constraints are baked into the slot choices so renders stay producible-adjacent.

The four things that make a knit buildable and that a Flux pixel cannot specify: yarn count + fibre + blend ratio (filled by T2 yarn), true gauge GG + stitch density (T2 + T3 + a PPS swatch), panel shaping + stitch-count grade (the T3 CAD programmer), and finished measurements + tolerances + shrinkage allowance (the sizing math into the tech pack).

The three things Flux actively renders wrong that a human must catch before money moves: impossible knits (non-stitch-conserving cables, ribs that change wale count, un-linkable seams), un-payable colourwork (a 6-colour jacquard the 2-4-colour dye-lot budget cannot fund), and pill-prone acrylic surfaces (a gorgeous brushed-fuzzy A2 render that is a return machine).

Flux-dev/schnell are guidance-distilled, so they prefer descriptive prose over keyword-salad and ignore true negative prompts on the default path; the distilled guidance ~3.0-3.8 dial controls how tightly a render follows the stitch/colour brief, and every defect avoidance must be phrased as a positive description of the correct state.

The disciplined sweep where the seed is fixed and exactly one slot (stitch, then colour, then fit) is changed at a time so the visual change is attributable, with every keeper logged as prompt + seed + guidance + steps + model + dimensions, versus sweeping the seed only to explore directions.

Making A1/A2/A3 read as one line despite Flux having no garment memory across calls, by reusing identical styling/shot/lighting/render-control slots verbatim, forcing shared cream/oat/charcoal anchor tokens, holding a seed family, and optionally feeding a hero image via img2img/IP-Adapter/Redux if the endpoint exposes it; a brand-look goal, not a spec-identity guarantee.

The load-bearing seam where design hands off to T2 and T3: choose a direction on the on-model render, re-render flat-lay + tech-flat, human-review against the four constraints and three traps, map intent onto the upstream specs, have the CAD programmer author the program, validate on a physical PPS swatch as ground truth, lock the tech pack, and let the pop-ups set the size curve.

A 0-1 readiness gate for a design before sampling, computed as constraints-met x traps-avoided x PPS-validated, where each factor is the fraction of the four constraints satisfied, the fraction of the three traps avoided, and the PPS-validation state (0 un-swatched, partial under test, 1 a passing physical swatch); a low factor on any axis caps the whole score so a pretty but un-payable or un-swatched render cannot read as ready.

The UNKNOWN, owned by no upstream file, of the specific live micro-trends, slang, sounds, and local hype objects of Turlock/Central-Valley youth in mid-2026; refused rather than fabricated, with estimated channels (TikTok FYP, IG Reels, Pinterest, Depop, the CSU-Stanislaus and bilingual social graph) and closed by a listening loop plus pop-up recon plus own-channel sell-through before a name or content calendar ships.

The release clock reconciling the California sell-window (light/transitional ~Sept-April, heavy wool only Nov-Feb), the Ludhiana production clock (yarn-in -> ex-factory ~6-12 wks, avoid the Jul-Oct cluster peak), and the trend clock (accents picked 1-2 quarters ahead): D1 Fall core (A1), D2 Holiday premium (A3), D3 Youth accent (A2), D4 Spring transitional (A1-light).

nodes.definition: Fix what Flux IS and IS NOT in this pipeline, because the framing prevents the most expensive mistake. Flux sits at the front of the generative-design->simulation->virtual-sampling chain, upstream of the CAD/flat-knit programmer: it IS a near-zero-marginal-cost visual-ideation, mood, and content engine, and the act of generating is itself the 'AI-designed, made by hands' marketing asset. It IS NOT a CAD/knit programmer, gauge calculator, grading engine, or any guarantee the rendered knit is knittable - a Flux image has no stitch count, no GG, no yarn count, no measurement, and no shrinkage behaviour, and will happily render an impossible knit. The brand-specific stake: mistaking a Flux image for a spec ships an un-producible tech pack to Ludhiana and burns a ~2-5 wk sampling cycle plus dye-lot money [ESTIMATE: method = sampling-lead-time from yarn deep-dive x dye-lot cost, MED]. Flux de-risks the idea; it does not de-risk the make.

included: the un-producible-tech-pack mistake and its sampling+dye-lot cost
excluded: the buildability inputs the pixel lacks (its own node)

pros.claim: Naming the idea-engine vs compiler boundary up front stops every downstream over-trust of a render
pros.example: the owner banks a beautiful on-model A3 as a content asset but does not send it to Ludhiana as a spec

cons.claim: Over-stating the limit can make the owner under-use a genuinely powerful ideation tool
cons.example: refusing to let Flux drive concept selection because it 'is not a spec' wastes its real cheap-ideation value

failure_modes: treating a render as a producible spec and shipping it to the factory
dismissing Flux as a toy and losing the cheap-ideation and content value
acceptance_tests: Flux is stated as an upstream idea/content engine and explicitly not a compiler/gauge/grading engine, and the un-producible-tech-pack mistake with its sampling+dye-lot cost is named as an estimate
revisit_triggers: a new Flux capability (e.g. native stitch/measurement output) appears
the AI-autonomy test resolves the make-side limit
the sampling-cycle or dye-lot cost basis is refreshed

base.update_signal: a Flux capability shift or a refreshed sampling/dye-lot cost basis changes the framing

nodes.definition: Encode the four fixed upstream constraints into the prompt so generations stay producible-adjacent rather than being re-derived from taste: (1) colour budget <=2-4 launch colours, from the dye-lot MOQ ~150-500 kg/colour [ESTIMATE: yarn deep-dive, MED-HIGH] -> interest comes from stitch + silhouette, not colour-count, and the prompt forces shared cream/oat/charcoal anchors with at most one accent; (2) 12GG warm-California weight ~200-350 g -> the gauge slot says 'fine 12-gauge, tight even stitches, lightweight' and fakes substance with surface stitch (cable, half-Milano), never bulky yarn; (3) linking is the throughput bottleneck -> favour fewer/cleaner seams, reserve fashioning marks as an A3 cue; (4) anti-pill is a brand-ending gate on acrylic A2 -> the A2 prompt forces a smooth tight surface and forbids brushed/floated looks. The design rule that falls out: texture-over-colour, silhouette-over-print, single-colour body with at most a contrast rib/tip.

included: the four constraints as prompt-shaping rules
excluded: the yarn/dye-lot mechanics behind the constraints

pros.claim: Baking constraints into slot choices keeps renders inside the buildable/payable envelope from the first prompt
pros.example: forcing two anchors + one accent stops Flux proposing a six-colour Fair-Isle the budget cannot fund

cons.claim: Hard-coding constraints into prompts can prune a genuinely sellable idea before the trap-review stage
cons.example: an over-tight colour rule kills a two-accent drop that the budget could in fact carry once a hero proves out

failure_modes: prompting from a moodboard and ignoring the colour/gauge/seam/pill constraints
treating the constraints as aesthetics rather than as the producibility envelope
acceptance_tests: all four constraints are each tied to a specific prompt-slot consequence and the texture-over-colour design rule is stated as the spine
revisit_triggers: a dye-lot MOQ or colour-budget change
a gauge or weight-band change
the anti-pill or linker constraint is relaxed or tightened upstream

base.update_signal: an upstream constraint (colour budget, gauge, seam, anti-pill) changes

nodes.definition: Give the eight-slot prompt skeleton, ordered to lead with the garment and end with render controls, each slot pulling a specific upstream vocabulary: (1) garment + silhouette/fit (crew/mock/cardigan/quarter-zip; soft-boxy/relaxed-straight/slightly-cropped; dropped shoulder; ~5-6in ease look) from the design deep-dive; (2) knit construction + stitch (FF look, visible stitch; 2x2 rib full-body, half-Milano, cable, links-links, pointelle, jersey, plating; fashioning marks on A3) from the glossary; (3) gauge look ('fine 12-gauge, tight even stitches, lightweight' - gauge as visible stitch size, never a number Flux understands) from yarn; (4) colour + fibre/blend hand (the 2-4-colour palette; 'matte soft cotton-blend', 'lustrous fine merino', 'smooth matte acrylic' - Flux renders hand/sheen, not fibre identity) from yarn; (5) styling + model/no-model (gender-neutral worn open/layered, or flat-lay, or tech-flat; California-casual); (6) shot type (pick ONE); (7) photography + lighting (soft natural daylight, warm Californian light, neutral backdrop, never alpine - or Flux gives you Aspen); (8) render controls (positive-phrased quality + defect avoidance). Flux is guidance-distilled, so descriptive prose beats keyword-salad.

pros.claim: An ordered eight-slot skeleton makes a prompt repeatable and forces every render to encode the upstream spec vocabulary
pros.example: the gauge slot always reads 'fine 12-gauge tight even stitches' so no render drifts to a chunky 5GG look

cons.claim: A fixed slot order can over-constrain creative exploration on early ideation sweeps
cons.example: rigidly filling all eight slots on a broad explore wastes the cheap-tier freedom to find an unexpected silhouette

failure_modes: keyword-salad prompting that the distilled model handles poorly
dropping the lighting slot and getting an alpine/cabin default that violates the brand read
acceptance_tests: all eight slots are listed in order, each tied to its upstream-vocabulary source, with the descriptive-prose-over-keyword-salad rule stated
revisit_triggers: a new stitch or silhouette enters the line vocabulary
a Flux version changes prompt-adherence behaviour
the lighting/brand-read preset is revised

nodes.definition: Map each Flux shot type to the job it does, and run all three at different stages. On-model lookbook -> concept selection + content (most sell-y, but hides construction, hands are the #1 defect source, fit is only implied). Flat-lay / ghost-mannequin -> read the actual garment shape, proportion, stitch, and colour for spec hand-off (proportions visual, still no measurements). Tech-flat / CAD-style front+back -> the closest Flux gets to a spec drawing, but an illustration not CAD, to be treated as a sketch to redraw properly. The workflow order: on-model to choose a direction and make content, then flat-lay + tech-flat of the chosen direction to read it for hand-off - appealing shot first, buildable shot second. Pick exactly ONE shot type per prompt (slot 6).

excluded: the eight-step image->spec bridge that consumes the shots (IMAGE_TO_SPEC_BRIDGE)

pros.claim: Assigning a job to each shot type prevents an on-model beauty shot being mistaken for a spec drawing
pros.example: the owner selects direction on-model but only reads proportion off the flat-lay before hand-off

cons.claim: Running three shot types per direction multiplies render cost and time
cons.example: generating on-model + flat-lay + tech-flat for every candidate before culling burns endpoint budget

failure_modes: reading fit off an on-model shot where fit is only implied
annotating a tech-flat illustration directly as if it were CAD
acceptance_tests: each of the three shot types is tied to its job (concept/content, shape-for-handoff, sketch-not-CAD) and the appealing-first/buildable-second order is stated

nodes.definition: Set the render params, all [SNAPSHOT] to re-confirm on the owner's live endpoint/version. Guidance (distilled CFG) ~3.0-3.8 (~3.5 balance; higher -> tighter brief adherence/flatter texture, lower -> natural texture/looser brief; tech-flats can push 3.5-5) - the key 'did it follow my stitch/colour brief' dial. Steps ~24-32 (diminishing returns past ~32; low end for sweeps, high for finals). Dimensions multiples of 32, ~768-1024/side - portrait 832x1216 on-model, square 1024x1024 flat-lay, landscape for capsule group shots. Seed = fix to iterate one variable, sweep to explore. Model tier: schnell for cheap ideation sweeps -> dev for the working look -> pro for the hero/content final. The iteration discipline: broad-explore at 5-10 seeds, then LOCK the seed and sweep ONE slot (stitch, then colour, then fit) so the change is attributable, tune guidance for fidelity, finalize on the good tier, and log prompt+seed+guidance+steps+model+dims with every keeper or 'you've made art, not a process'. [FACT - Flux guides; SNAPSHOT on exact numbers]

included: the seed-locked one-variable sweep and logging discipline

pros.claim: Snapshot param ranges plus seed-locked one-variable iteration make the render process attributable and cheap-to-iterate
pros.example: fixing the seed and sweeping rib->half-Milano->cable isolates which stitch the change came from

cons.claim: Published param ranges drift across Flux versions, so a fixed recipe silently goes stale
cons.example: a guidance value tuned on one dev build over-bakes texture on the next

failure_modes: feeding a stale param value into spend without re-confirming on the live endpoint
random re-rolls instead of seed-locked one-variable sweeps, losing attribution
acceptance_tests: guidance ~3.0-3.8, steps ~24-32, dimension/model-tier guidance, and the fix-seed-sweep-one-slot + logging discipline are stated, all tagged snapshot
revisit_triggers: a Flux model version or endpoint changes the param behaviour

nodes.definition: Steer defects out with positive phrasing because the guidance-distilled dev/schnell path ignores true negative prompts - every avoidance is a positive description of the correct state. Distorted hands / extra fingers: not 'no deformed hands' but 'accurate hands, five separated fingers, relaxed at sides or in pockets' - or sidestep with hands in pockets / crop out / flat-lay (the cheapest hand fix is no hands in frame, and hands are the #1 on-model defect). Fake logos / garbled text: not 'no logos' but 'plain unbranded garment, smooth fabric, no text, no logos, no labels, no graphics' (also dodging the TM/right-of-publicity exposure). Impossible / non-knittable knit: cannot be negative-prompted because it is a knowledge gap not a render flag - constrain positively to real structures ('regular 2x2 rib', 'standard evenly-repeated cable') and catch the impossible ones in human spec review, not the prompt. Advanced true_cfg_scale>1 with a real negative exists but ~doubles compute and is rarely needed if positive phrasing + shot choice are disciplined. [FACT - guidance-distilled behaviour; SNAPSHOT]

included: the true_cfg_scale escape hatch and its cost
excluded: the human spec review that catches impossible knits (FLUX_TRAPS, IMAGE_TO_SPEC_BRIDGE)

pros.claim: Phrasing every avoidance as a positive correct-state cue actually steers the distilled model where negatives do nothing
pros.example: 'five separated fingers relaxed in pockets' fixes hands that 'no deformed hands' leaves broken

cons.claim: Positive phrasing cannot fix a knowledge gap like an impossible knit, so it can create false confidence the render is clean
cons.example: 'standard evenly-repeated cable' still yields a non-stitch-conserving cable that only review catches

failure_modes: writing true negative prompts that the distilled path ignores
assuming positive phrasing alone makes a render producible without the human trap-review
acceptance_tests: the ignored-negatives behaviour is stated and positive rewrites are given for hands, logos/text, and impossible-knit (the last routed to human review)
revisit_triggers: a Flux version changes negative-prompt handling
the true_cfg_scale path becomes cheap enough to use routinely

nodes.definition: Engineer capsule consistency, because Flux has no garment memory across calls. Make A1/A2/A3 read as one line by: reusing identical slots 5-8 (styling + shot + lighting + render controls) verbatim, varying only slots 1-4; forcing shared cream/oat/charcoal anchor tokens that mirror the real shared-dye-lot economics; holding a seed family; and optionally feeding a hero image via img2img/IP-Adapter/Redux/'context' IF the endpoint exposes it ([SNAPSHOT/UNKNOWN] per endpoint - verify first). The honest limit: consistency is a brand-look goal (achievable), not a spec-identity guarantee (not achievable) - spec identity comes from the tech pack, not the image set. After the three articles are chosen, run a capsule-consistency pass that reuses the identical lighting/backdrop/model/render-control text, holds the same seed family, forces the shared anchors, and renders the group/flat-lay capsule shot (landscape AR) for the lookbook.

included: the capsule-consistency pass and group shot
excluded: the tech pack that owns spec identity (IMAGE_TO_SPEC_BRIDGE)

pros.claim: Reusing fixed slots + anchors + a seed family makes a three-article render set read as one cohesive line
pros.example: the same daylight preset and cream anchor across A1/A2/A3 produces a lookbook that hangs together

cons.claim: Image-level consistency can be mistaken for spec consistency, hiding that each garment still needs its own tech pack
cons.example: a cohesive lookbook tempts the owner to treat the capsule as spec-locked when only the look is locked

failure_modes: assuming consistency means the garments share a buildable spec
relying on img2img/IP-Adapter without verifying the endpoint exposes it
acceptance_tests: the shared-scaffold/anchor/seed-family/optional-img2img method is given and the brand-look-goal vs spec-identity-guarantee limit is stated explicitly

nodes.definition: Define the eight-step translation workflow from a Flux image to a knittable garment - the seam where design hands off to T2 + T3. (1) Choose direction from the on-model render (bank as content). (2) Re-render flat-lay + tech-flat of that direction. (3) Human review vs the four constraints + three traps - kill impossible/un-payable/pill-prone features NOW. (4) Map intent onto the upstream specs - the fibre x count x gauge x weight quadruple, stitch from the glossary, finished-measurement base + grade. (5) CAD/flat-knit programmer authors the program - needle actions, FF shaping, the stitch-count grade (human + machine-specific Shima APEX / Stoll M1plus, never the image). (6) Physical PPS swatch + sample = ground truth - measures real gauge/density/shrinkage, confirms ICI pilling >=3-4 post-wash; the swatch, not the render, is truth. (7) Lock the tech pack - measurements + tolerances + count/shade + GSM + stitch + trims + AQL. (8) Pop-up fit calibration sets the size curve - the render never touches this, body data does. The one-line rule: the Flux image gets you blank-page -> approved look + content; the tech pack + PPS swatch + programmer get you approved-look -> knittable garment; never skip the second half because the first was cheap and pretty.

nodes.definition: Define the recomputing producibility-readiness gate for a design before sampling, so any render's readiness regenerates exactly from three factors: readiness = constraints_met x traps_avoided x PPS_validated, each on 0-1, multiplied so a low factor on any axis caps the whole score (a pretty but un-payable or un-swatched render cannot read as ready). constraints_met = (number of the four constraints satisfied) / 4 [colour <=2-4, 12GG weight, few-seam, anti-pill]. traps_avoided = (number of the three traps cleared) / 3 [impossible-knit, un-payable-colourwork, pill-prone-acrylic]. PPS_validated in {0 = un-swatched, 0.5 = swatch under test, 1 = a passing physical PPS swatch (gauge/density/shrinkage measured, ICI pilling >=3-4 post-wash)}. Worked checks: a render meeting all 4 constraints, clearing all 3 traps, but un-swatched = 1.0 x 1.0 x 0.0 = 0.00 (NOT ready - the swatch is the gate); meeting 4/4, clearing 2/3 traps, swatch under test = 1.0 x 0.667 x 0.5 = 0.33; meeting 4/4, clearing 3/3, passing swatch = 1.0 x 1.0 x 1.0 = 1.00 (ready). The score is advisory for sequencing sampling spend, never a substitute for the PPS swatch verdict it already requires at full weight.

revisit_triggers: the constraint set or trap list changes the factor denominators
the PPS-validation states are redefined
the score is found to mis-rank sampling priority

base.update_signal: the constraint set, trap list, or PPS-validation states change the formula

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the Flux method current. A per-drop cadence (re-run the method each drop cycle) plus material-change triggers that send the owner back through the relevant nodes: a new Flux model version or endpoint param behaviour (re-confirm FLUX_PARAMS and the template footer); a re-confirmed or changed trend accent at an order-by date (re-run TREND_FILTER_FUNNEL -> DROP_CALENDAR); a PPS swatch result on gauge/density/shrinkage/pilling (re-run BUILDABILITY_INPUTS and re-score READINESS_SCORE); an AI design->knit-program autonomy test result (update AUTONOMY_UNKNOWN and possibly the bridge step 5); pop-up trend recon or own-channel sell-through (close HYPE_SIGNAL_GAP and bias styling/colour); a legal change to right-of-publicity / Lanham / Class-25 (re-check LEGAL_RENDER_GUARDRAIL). Without this loop the snapshot params silently go stale, the perishable trend accent drifts, and the un-tested autonomy assumption hardens into a planning fact. Every keeper render and its log feed the next cycle.

included: the material-change trigger list and the node each re-runs

pros.claim: A trigger list routing each change back to its node keeps snapshot params, perishable accents, and the autonomy assumption from silently going stale
pros.example: a new Flux version fires the loop and re-confirms FLUX_PARAMS before the next drop's spend

cons.claim: A per-drop cadence can over-refresh stable nodes that only change across versions
cons.example: re-running the whole eight-slot skeleton each drop when only the accent moved wastes effort

failure_modes: letting snapshot params or a perishable accent age silently past their validity
ignoring a fired trigger (new autonomy test result) and planning on stale assumptions
acceptance_tests: a per-drop cadence and a material-change trigger list each routing to its node (FLUX_PARAMS, TREND_FILTER_FUNNEL/DROP_CALENDAR, BUILDABILITY_INPUTS/READINESS_SCORE, AUTONOMY_UNKNOWN, HYPE_SIGNAL_GAP, LEGAL_RENDER_GUARDRAIL) exist
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse for how the inputs actually update

base.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

conflict_axes.name: idea_engine_vs_spec_authority
conflict_axes.description: A cheap, pretty Flux render carries real design intent yet zero buildability numbers, so trusting it as a spec and trusting only the tech pack pull opposite ways.
poles: treat the render as the approved spec
treat only the tech pack + swatch as the spec
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the render gets blank-page->approved look + content; the tech pack + PPS swatch + programmer get approved-look->knittable garment; never let the image author a buildability number

conflict_axes.name: photogenic_vs_producible
conflict_axes.description: The most beautiful render is often the un-payable, impossible, or pill-prone one, so visual appeal and producibility point opposite ways.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run the three-trap review and the constraint check on every chosen render; down-rate a beautiful but un-payable/impossible/pill-prone look no matter how good it looks

conflict_axes.name: constraint_encoding_vs_creative_freedom
conflict_axes.description: Baking the four constraints into every prompt keeps renders buildable but can prune a sellable idea before the trap-review stage.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: encode constraints on the working and final sweeps but allow a cheap-tier broad explore to surface unexpected directions, then re-impose the constraints before hand-off

conflict_axes.name: true_negatives_vs_positive_phrasing
conflict_axes.description: Practitioners reach for negative prompts to remove defects, but the guidance-distilled path ignores them, so the instinct and the working method diverge.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: phrase every defect avoidance as a positive correct-state cue, reserve true_cfg_scale negatives for the rare case its doubled compute is worth it

conflict_axes.name: capsule_look_vs_spec_identity
conflict_axes.description: Engineered render consistency makes A1/A2/A3 look like one line, which can be mistaken for a shared buildable spec.
poles: treat a consistent lookbook as spec-locked
treat only the per-garment tech pack as identity
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: consistency is a brand-look goal (achievable); spec identity comes from each garment's tech pack, never from the image set

conflict_axes.name: ai_autonomy_assumed_vs_tested
conflict_axes.description: The pipeline tempts an assumption that AI outputs a runnable knit program, while the honest state is that autonomy on our fabrics is untested.
poles: hold autonomy UNKNOWN and test it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold autonomy UNKNOWN, keep a human programmer + PPS swatch closing the loop, and let a test result, not an assumption, update the node

conflict_axes.name: trend_chase_vs_constraint_decline
conflict_axes.description: A live micro-trend can demand six colours or a brushed-pill surface the colour-starved anti-pill line cannot make, so trend pull and constraint fit diverge.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: only signals surviving all three filters AND fitting the four constraints enter the line; a six-colour or brushed-pill trend is read, noted, and declined

conflict_axes.name: hype_signal_guess_vs_refusal
conflict_axes.description: A hype-adjacent name and trend-native content want a Central-Valley-youth signal that is genuinely unknown, tempting a fabricated guess.
poles: refuse it and run an instrument
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: refuse the unknown specifics, run a listening loop + pop-up recon + sell-through, and pin the signal before any name or content calendar ships

conflict_axes.name: render_safety_assumed_vs_legal_exposure
conflict_axes.description: An AI render feels legally free because a model drew it, but a real-person likeness, logo, or un-cleared slogan-knit imports the same publicity/endorsement/TM exposure.
poles: treat renders as legally identical to any asset
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep every render plain/unbranded and every name original/coined and Spanish-cleared; the model drawing it grants no legal shortcut

edge_cases.description: A beautiful on-model render is sent to Ludhiana as a spec with no tech pack
edge_cases.trigger: an approved look is treated as a buildable spec because it is cheap and pretty
edge_cases.mitigation: route the look through the eight-step bridge; only a tech pack + PPS swatch + programmer produce a knittable garment

edge_cases.description: A render's apparent gauge, count, or measurement is read off the pixels as the spec
edge_cases.trigger: a buildability number is inferred from a render instead of from its named owner
edge_cases.mitigation: fill yarn count from T2, true GG/density from the PPS swatch, grade from the T3 programmer, measurements from the sizing math - never from the image

edge_cases.description: A gorgeous brushed-fuzzy A2 acrylic render is chosen for its looks
edge_cases.trigger: a fuzzy/brushed surface render wins on beauty for the acrylic value article
edge_cases.mitigation: reject the fuzzy render for A2 - one pilling video is brand-ending; force a smooth crisp tight surface and the anti-pill grade

edge_cases.description: A rendered A3 cable that does not conserve stitches is shipped as knittable
edge_cases.trigger: an impossible-knit cable or mis-placed fashioning mark passes review
edge_cases.mitigation: have the spec reviewer + programmer verify cable stitch-conservation and price the extra yarn + linker time before sampling

edge_cases.description: AI is assumed to output a runnable knit program, skipping the human programmer and swatch
edge_cases.trigger: an un-tested autonomy assumption is treated as a planning fact
edge_cases.mitigation: hold autonomy UNKNOWN, keep a human programmer + PPS swatch closing the loop, and run the test before assuming

edge_cases.description: A six-colour jacquard render is approved against the 2-4-colour dye-lot budget
edge_cases.trigger: an un-payable colourwork render passes the colour-budget gate
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the colour-budget constraint at review and decline the un-fundable colourwork

edge_cases.description: True negative prompts are written to remove a defect on Flux-dev and silently do nothing
edge_cases.trigger: a 'no deformed hands / no logos' negative is relied on for defect removal
edge_cases.mitigation: rewrite every avoidance as a positive correct-state cue or sidestep (hands in pockets, flat-lay)

edge_cases.description: A stale snapshot param value is fed into spend on a new Flux version
edge_cases.trigger: a guidance/steps value tuned on an old build is reused without re-confirmation
edge_cases.mitigation: re-confirm the param ranges on the live endpoint each version change before any spend

edge_cases.description: The Central-Valley-youth hype signal is fabricated to feed a name or content calendar
edge_cases.trigger: an unknown local trend specific is guessed rather than instrumented
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse the unknown specifics, run the listening loop + pop-up recon + sell-through, and pin before any name or content ships

edge_cases.description: A launch drop is committed into the Jul-Oct Ludhiana cluster peak
edge_cases.trigger: a drop's order-by date lands inside the peak-contention window
edge_cases.mitigation: order ahead of the peak (D1 by May-Jun, D2 by Jul-Aug pre-peak) and keep the land date out of the peak shadow

edge_cases.description: An AI render of a real-person likeness or a logo wordmark is published as marketing
edge_cases.trigger: a render imports right-of-publicity / endorsement / trademark exposure because it feels AI-safe
edge_cases.mitigation: keep renders plain/unbranded and names original/coined and Spanish-cleared; the model drawing it grants no legal shortcut

dominance_rules.rule: The tech pack + PPS swatch dominate any pressure to treat a render as a spec
dominance_rules.rationale: a Flux pixel carries no buildability number, so an over-trusted render ships an un-producible tech pack
dominance_rules.trigger: a beautiful render is about to be sent to the factory as the spec
dominance_rules.action: route it through the eight-step bridge; let the tech pack + PPS swatch + programmer, not the image, define the make

dominance_rules.rule: Producibility dominates beauty when they conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: the most beautiful render is often the un-payable, impossible, or pill-prone one
dominance_rules.trigger: a chosen render is gorgeous but trips a constraint or a trap
dominance_rules.action: down-rate it; pick the render that clears the three traps and the four constraints even if it is less striking

dominance_rules.rule: The PPS swatch verdict dominates the readiness score it feeds
dominance_rules.rationale: the score is advisory and already requires the swatch at full weight
dominance_rules.trigger: a high readiness score is treated as a producibility verdict
dominance_rules.action: treat the score as sampling-sequencing only; a passing physical swatch is the real gate

dominance_rules.rule: Positive phrasing dominates true negative prompts on Flux-dev
dominance_rules.rationale: the guidance-distilled path ignores true negatives
dominance_rules.trigger: a defect is being removed with a negative prompt
dominance_rules.action: rewrite the avoidance as a positive correct-state cue or sidestep it via shot choice

dominance_rules.rule: The four constraints dominate a trend signal that violates them
dominance_rules.rationale: a colour-starved anti-pill fine-gauge line cannot make a six-colour or brushed-pill trend
dominance_rules.trigger: a surviving micro-trend needs >4 colours or a pill-prone surface
dominance_rules.action: read it, note it, and decline it; only constraint-fitting signals enter the line

dominance_rules.rule: Refusal dominates fabrication on the Central-Valley-youth hype signal
dominance_rules.rationale: the specifics are genuinely unknown and a guess would mis-steer a name or content
dominance_rules.trigger: a local hype specific is needed for a name or content calendar
dominance_rules.action: refuse the unknown, run the listening loop + pop-up recon + sell-through, and pin before shipping

dominance_rules.rule: The test result dominates any assumed AI->knit-program autonomy
dominance_rules.rationale: autonomy on our fabrics is UNKNOWN and must be tested not assumed
dominance_rules.trigger: the pipeline is planned as if AI outputs a runnable program
dominance_rules.action: keep a human programmer + PPS swatch closing the loop until a test result proves otherwise

dominance_rules.rule: The legal guardrail dominates a render's apparent AI-safety
dominance_rules.rationale: a real-person likeness, logo, or un-cleared slogan imports the same publicity/endorsement/TM exposure regardless of how it was drawn
dominance_rules.trigger: a render contains a real-person likeness, a logo, or an un-Spanish-cleared slogan-knit
dominance_rules.action: keep renders plain/unbranded and names original/coined/Spanish-cleared; the model drawing it grants no shortcut

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged snapshot param dominates a confident render-spend built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: param ranges drift across Flux versions and cannot carry more certainty than their snapshot
dominance_rules.trigger: a stale param value is about to drive render spend on a new version
dominance_rules.action: re-confirm the param on the live endpoint before committing spend

anti_rework_rules.rule: Frame Flux as an idea engine and name the four missing buildability inputs before any render is treated as a spec
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a render-as-spec hand-off that ships an un-producible tech pack and burns a sampling cycle plus dye-lot money

anti_rework_rules.rule: Encode the four constraints into the prompt at authoring time, not after a render is chosen
anti_rework_rules.prevents: generating beautiful but un-payable/un-makeable renders that must be discarded and re-prompted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the three-trap review on a chosen render before mapping intent onto the upstream specs
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an impossible-knit, un-payable, or pill-prone feature surfacing only after sampling spend

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log prompt + seed + guidance + steps + model + dims with every keeper render
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an un-reproducible keeper that must be re-derived from scratch when a variant is needed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold AI->knit-program autonomy UNKNOWN and budget a human programmer + swatch from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a programmer-free plan that collapses at the design->program hand-off and must be re-staffed mid-drop

anti_rework_rules.rule: Validate gauge/density/shrinkage on a physical PPS swatch before locking the tech pack
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a tech pack built on a render's apparent gauge that fails at bulk and forces a re-spec

anti_rework_rules.rule: Re-confirm the perishable trend accent at each drop's order-by date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ordering a stale accent colour that misses the season and becomes markdown

anti_rework_rules.rule: Re-confirm snapshot params on the live endpoint when the Flux version changes
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a drop's render spend running on stale param values that over-bake or under-follow the brief

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep every render plain/unbranded and every name original/coined/Spanish-cleared the first time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later legal sweep that must re-render or re-name assets that already imported publicity/endorsement/TM exposure

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new Flux model version or endpoint changes param behaviour
iteration_protocol.action: re-confirm the guidance/steps/dimension ranges and the template footer before any render spend

iteration_protocol.trigger: a physical PPS swatch returns gauge/density/shrinkage/pilling results
iteration_protocol.action: fill the true buildability numbers, re-score readiness, and lock or revise the tech pack

iteration_protocol.trigger: an AI design->knit-program autonomy test returns a result on any fabric
iteration_protocol.action: update the autonomy node and, if proven, revise the programmer step of the bridge

iteration_protocol.trigger: a drop's order-by date arrives or a trend accent is re-confirmed/changed
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the trend funnel for the accent and re-schedule the affected drop

iteration_protocol.trigger: the listening loop, pop-up recon, or own-channel sell-through returns Central-Valley signal
iteration_protocol.action: close the hype-signal gap and bias styling/colour and any hype-adjacent name

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream constraint (colour budget, gauge, seam, anti-pill) changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-encode the constraints into the prompt and re-score readiness

iteration_protocol.trigger: a right-of-publicity / Lanham / Class-25 legal change or a new render use is proposed
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the render guardrail and adjust the plain/unbranded and naming rules

priority_rationale: The Flux role framing and the constraint encoding are foundational because the skeleton, params, steering, and every worked prompt read their producibility envelope from them; the skeleton, shot-type, params, steering, and consistency build the render method that the template and the three worked A1/A2/A3 prompts make immediately usable; the buildability inputs, the three traps, and the autonomy UNKNOWN are the load-bearing bridge layer that turns a render into a producible spec via T2/T3/PPS; trend filtering, the refused hype-signal gap, and the four-drop calendar schedule what may enter the line; the legal guardrail governs how every render and name may be expressed; and the image-to-spec bridge, the recomputing readiness score, and the review loop come last because they compose all upstream nodes into a hand-off, a sampling gate, and a self-correcting refresh.
